msa_bias_linearity — SPC msa op

• Data kinds: table → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.msa_bias_linearity(table, reference='reference', measured='measured') (to call the implementation directly, import spc; spc.msa_bias_linearity(table, reference='reference', measured='measured'); from the registry, opsspc.get("msa_bias_linearity"))

Usage

Bias against a reference value and how that bias depends on the reference (linearity) (table).

Regresses the bias bias = measured - reference on the reference value (bias = intercept + slope * reference). If the slope is not 0, the measurement system is off by a different amount depending on where in the measuring range it is = a linearity problem.

The result is the mean bias per reference value (ref / bias_mean / n), the regression's intercept / slope / each one's standard error, t value and p value, and the overall mean bias.

★ An exact property usable as a gate: given a noise-free bias = a + b*ref, least squares returns a and b exactly (residual 0). The standard error is then 0, so t is inf / p is 0 -- this is not a defect but the correct report of a perfect fit, so it is returned as is.
